log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought: Opponent has multiple Steel-types (Kingambit, Archaludon, Gholdengo) which Garchomp and Volcarona exploit heavily. Primarina covers opposing Garchomp and Incineroar defensively.

Incineroar's Intimidate weakens their physical attackers (Garchomp, Dragonite), and Fake Out helps lead. Garchomp brings fast Mega pressure and Stone Edge hits Volcarona. Gholdengo gives special coverage against Dragonite, Garchomp, and Primarina.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm weighing team options against their Dragonite, Gholdengo, Mimikyu, Garchomp, Volcarona, Primarina lineup. Incineroar's Intimidate helps against their physical threats like Dragonite and Garchomp, while I'm considering Garchomp with Mega and Rock-type coverage against Volcarona's Bug/Fire weakness.

Kingambit's Dark/Steel typing deals with Mimikyu well, though its Dark hits Volcarona only neutrally, and I'm checking how Gholdengo stacks up in a potential mirror matchup. I'm leaning toward Incineroar, Garchomp, and Gholdengo as a core for coverage against their Dragon and Steel-type threats.

decisions.thought: Garchomp easily outspeeds Incineroar even after Mega Evolving. Mega Earthquake provides massive STAB damage to offset the Intimidate drop and punish Incineroar or whatever switches in.

Opposing Garchomp is faster than Incineroar, and Fake Out has priority, so it's the only reliable way to act before it. Fake Out flinches it for a turn and chips damage, which is better than Parting Shot's extra Attack drop here.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: The opponent's Garchomp is faster than my Incineroar, but since Fake Out has priority, it'll still hit first and flinch Garchomp while dealing solid damage — a clear best move for turn 1.

decisions.thought: Mega Garchomp naturally outspeeds Incineroar. Even at -1 Attack, super-effective STAB Earthquake deals massive damage to Incineroar and punishes most switches like Archaludon or Kingambit.

Flare Blitz only hits the opposing Dragon/Ground Garchomp for half damage, and Incineroar's Fake Out is already spent. Parting Shot cuts its Attack to -2 before Incineroar pivots out, which reduces the damage its Earthquake can deal to whichever Pokémon comes in.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Opponent's Garchomp is at 87% HP with an attack drop from intimidate, plus sand force active and a possibly unknown item—maybe even Garchompite given this could be mega-capable format. I'm checking Flare Blitz's effectiveness: Fire against Dragon is resisted at 0.5x, but against Ground it's neutral, so overall it should hit for standard neutral damage on this Dragon/Ground typing.

Weighing Parting Shot options too—it would drop Garchomp's attack further while pivoting into Gholdengo, but Gholdengo's Steel/Ghost typing is quad-weak to Garchomp's Earthquake since Ground hits Steel for 2x. None of Gholdengo's moves (Shadow Ball, Make It Rain, Thunderbolt) are super effective back since Garchomp resists or is immune to most of them, so that swap seems risky defensively while offering little offensive payoff.

Considering switching in our own Garchomp instead, but opposing Garchomp's Earthquake would hit for 2x damage on it too since Dragon/Ground takes double from Ground moves. Parting Shot still looks like the best call overall—it weakens Garchomp's attack further and keeps us flexible even though Incineroar has to leave the field.

decisions.thought: Incineroar is at 70 HP with no Sitrus left and is being forced out. Opposing Garchomp is at -2 Attack, so its Earthquake is weakened. My Garchomp has 185 HP, outspeeds it, and can Mega and pressure it, while Gholdengo has no good hit into Dragon/Ground.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar sits at 70/202 HP with no item left after the Sitrus Berry activated, while Garchomp is at 87% with its Attack and Special Attack both dropped. I'm trying to work out how much another Earthquake would do given those stat drops and Garchomp's unclear item situation.

My legal actions are only switches, so Incineroar has to go - I'm deciding between bringing in my own mega Garchomp (Rough Skin) or Gholdengo. Gholdengo's moves are mostly neutral or resisted against the opposing Dragon/Ground Garchomp, while my Garchomp's own Earthquake could land super effectively, so I'm leaning toward that option while weighing the Earthquake weakness it would also take.

My Garchomp has far superior speed (169 vs their 92, especially with Mega boost) and takes nothing extra from their Earthquake since Ground isn't super effective against Ground or Dragon. With their Garchomp already at -2 attack, switching in my own Garchomp is the stronger play here.

decisions.thought: Mega Garchomp is at -2 Attack and naturally slower than base Garchomp (base 92 vs 102 Speed), making it vulnerable to an immediate KO. Primarina is immune to Dragon-type attacks and comfortably handles Garchomp.

Our Garchomp is likely faster than the opposing Garchomp, which is at -2 Attack, so its Earthquake is weak. Outrage is Dragon-type and hits Dragon/Ground Garchomp for 2x, which should be enough to knock it out without spending Mega Evolution.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Our Garchomp's debuffed attack weakens its Earthquake, but as the Mega it still outpaces the opponent's Garchomp in speed and can threaten with a strong STAB Outrage.

Mega Garchomp's Outrage hits at 2x effectiveness, and with the opponent at roughly 87% of 185 HP (~161), that should be enough for a likely KO. Mega evolving now seems like the right call since it boosts attack further and our Garchomp is already plenty fast.

Running the full damage calculation, Outrage with STAB and the atk boost comes out to roughly 256 before random variance, which is already enough for a knockout without mega evolution. Since confusion from Outrage is an acceptable tradeoff and the KO is secured regardless, it makes sense to save the mega evolution for later rather than use it here.

decisions.thought: Primarina threatens a direct OHKO on Garchomp with Moonblast. Even if Garchomp is not locked into Outrage, Moonblast is the safest and strongest play to punish it or anything switching in.

Primarina is Water/Fairy, so Earthquake is super effective and Outrage is useless against it. Mega Garchomp's extra Attack should make Earthquake a likely knockout, and Sand Force has no effect without sand.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Our Garchomp matches up against their Primarina, Water/Fairy type. Outrage won't work since Dragon moves are blocked by Fairy, and Ground is neutral against both Water and Fairy, so I need to think about a different attacking option.

Earthquake comes out super effective on the Water side while remaining neutral overall, and with Primarina's modest 80 HP and 74 base defense, a Mega Garchomp's Earthquake should be a reliable KO. Mega evolving gives the same raw power boost but Sand Force won't matter without sand active, so the choice mostly comes down to whether the stat boost alone is worth it here.

decisions.thought: Garchomp fainted, so I must switch. Gholdengo is at full HP, outspeeds Primarina (136 vs 60), and resists Moonblast as a Steel type. Incineroar would take a super-effective Fairy hit at 35% HP.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Garchomp down, I need to pick between Incineroar and Gholdengo against Primarina. Incineroar is weak to Moonblast since Fairy hits Dark super effectively, while Gholdengo's Steel typing isn't weak to Fairy, making it the safer switch.

Gholdengo also outspeeds Primarina significantly, and Thunderbolt or Make It Rain can hit Primarina's Water-Fairy typing hard while its already-damaged HP makes it vulnerable to a strong attack this turn.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo outspeeds Primarina (136 vs 60). Make It Rain is 2x super effective against Fairy-type Primarina, with STAB and Life Orb, so it should knock out the 47 HP Primarina before it moves.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking type matchups: Primarina is Water/Fairy, so Gholdengo's Steel move hits the Fairy side super effectively while staying neutral against Water, and Thunderbolt would double up on the Water typing.

Factoring STAB, Make It Rain comes out far ahead in damage output, and with Primarina sitting around 47 HP and Gholdengo outspeeding, that move should secure the KO.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo outspeeds Primarina and threatens an immediate KO with Make It Rain. Volcarona resists Steel, easily handles Gholdengo, and sweeps their remaining team.
Volcarona heavily outspeeds Gholdengo, and STAB super-effective Fiery Dance easily knocks it out from 90% HP.

Gholdengo outspeeds Volcarona (136 vs 100). Make It Rain was just "not very effective" because Steel is resisted by Fire. Shadow Ball is neutral with STAB and the best damage option at -2 SpA, and it should leave Volcarona in range for a follow-up KO.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Gholdengo is faster at 136 speed versus Volcarona's 100, and with -2 SpA still likely has an edge. I'm checking type matchups for Steel against Volcarona's Bug/Fire typing to see how the damage would play out.

Running the damage math, Shadow Ball at -2 SpA with STAB and Life Orb lands around 60-70 damage against Volcarona's roughly 93 remaining HP, so it's not quite a KO, while Make It Rain stays stuck as the weaker option since Steel isn't super effective against Bug.

Volcarona's Fire Blast wouldn't threaten Gholdengo much since Steel resists Fire, so that's not a major concern here.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo has fainted, so the only legal action is switching in Incineroar. I'll take it. Parting Shot or Flare Blitz can be considered next turn against Volcarona.
Incineroar is the opponent's final Pokémon and is sitting at only 34% HP. At +1 Special Attack, Bug Buzz easily secures the knockout to win the match.

Volcarona is faster than Incineroar, but its Fire-type Fiery Dance is resisted by Incineroar's Fire typing, so Incineroar should survive the hit at 70 HP. Flare Blitz from Incineroar's high Attack should then knock out the 53% Volcarona. Fake Out fails on a Pokémon already on the field, so it is out.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm noting Volcarona resists Fire as a Bug/Fire type, so Incineroar's Flare Blitz wouldn't be very effective against it, and checking whether Fake Out still works despite that matchup since it only lands on the first turn out.

Parting Shot would drop Incineroar's Atk/SpA further and swap it out for a bench mon like Garchomp, which is relevant since Ground-type Earthquake hits Volcarona for 2x damage as a Fire type — meaning a healthy Garchomp could likely finish off Volcarona at its current HP, especially factoring in speed comparisons between the two.

Alternatively, I'm weighing whether Volcarona should Protect here instead, since Incineroar's Flare Blitz is only neutral/weak against Bug/Fire typing and might not do enough combined with Fiery Dance being resisted by Incineroar's Fire/Dark typing, so the exchange may not favor Incineroar as much as it initially seems.
